answer.rationale: Write-path p99 began climbing ~30 minutes after the deploy and is now 5x, which is the strongest actionable correlation among the three simultaneous facts. memory_b1 is the closest prior: rollback removed a post-release checkout failure and the prior build stayed stable without dropping customer writes. That matches the objective better than failover (no regional signal), read-replica routing (this load is settlement writes, not dashboards), or a circuit breaker (fail-fast can shed customer writes). memory_b6 cuts the other way: staged canaries have historically surfaced bad builds within an hour, so it is still uncertain the new release is causal versus peak write saturation. Verifying b1 and b6 before treating either as settled. Flagging downstream value risk because a write-path change during daily settlement peak can disrupt in-flight money movement if the rollback is the wrong lever. Keeping scale below a full-blast cut until those records are checked.
